experiment_data.hypothesis: At r=0.2 (20% real data), spectral collapse will manifest within 5 generations (log_det decline), unlike r=0.5 where decompression persisted through 10 gen (exp_006). This establishes a critical real-data ratio r_crit between 0.2 and 0.5 below which SLV-based collapse detection becomes viable. If controller triggers, it validates C3 claim that SLV can guide closed-loop mixing at low real-data budgets.

spec.description: Phase 1: Fixed mix r=0.2 ablation (20% real + 80% synthetic), seed 42, 5 generations
spec.command: bash -c "source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base && cd /root/spectral_collapse_ews && CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 python run_phase1.py --condition fixed_mix --seed 42 --generations 5 --signal log_det --tau 0.002 --k 0 --signal_mode per_gen --real_ratio 0.2 --gpu 0"
spec.data_count: 50K real pool, total_per_gen=50K (10K real + 40K synthetic per gen)
